Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Nov-2024 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. (INFORMATION ECHNOLOGY) EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER / DECEMBER 2024  
  SUBJECT: ICT 2124/ICT_2124 - PRINCIPLES OF DATA COMMUNICATION  
  PRINCIPLES OF DATA COMMUNICATION [ICT 2124]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               A microwave transmitter has an output of 0.1 W at 2 GHz. Assume that this transmitter is used in a     (5)  
  microwave communication system where the transmitting and receiving antennas are parabolas,  
  each 1.2 m in diameter.  
  i) What is the gain of each antenna in decibels?  
  ii) Considering antenna gain, what is the effective radiated power of the transmitted signal?  
  iii) If the receiving antenna is located 24 km from the transmitting antenna over a free space path,  
  find the available signal power out of the receiving antenna in dBm units.  
1B)               Apply Statistical Time Division Multiplexing (STDM) to a packet-switched network where users           (3)  
  transmit data at variable rates. Explain how STDM dynamically allocates time slots based on user  
  demand and improves bandwidth utilization compared to synchronous TDM.  
1C)               Compare the performance of the IEEE 802.5 (Token Ring) protocol with the CSMA/CD protocol              (2)  
  used in Ethernet.  
2A)               Encode the binary word 11001 using an even-parity Hamming code.                                        (5)  
2B)               Assume that a telephone line channel is equalized to allow bandpass data transmission over a           (3)  
  frequency range of 600 to 3000 Hz. The available bandwidth is 2400 Hz. For r=1, evaluate the  
  required bandwidth for 2400 bps QPSK and 4800-bps, eight level multilevel signalling. Is the  
  bandwidth adequate?  
2C)               Apply Frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM) to a system where three channels, each occupying 5         (2)  
  MHz, must be transmitted over a 20 MHz bandwidth. Explain how FDM divides the available  
  bandwidth and prevents interference between channels.  
3A)               Depict the communication between a transmitter (A) and a receiver (B) using the HDLC protocol          (5)  
  with selective reject ARQ, assuming a window size of 5. The following events take place:  
  
  i) A initializes the link, and B acknowledges the initialization.  
  ii) B transmits the first four data frames (Frame 1 to Frame 4).  
  iii) Frame 3 is damaged during transmission, and A sends a reject (REJ) for Frame 3.  
  iv) The REJ frame sent by A is lost, and B does not know about the rejection.  
  v) B experiences a timeout due to the missing acknowledgment for Frame 3 and retransmits the  
  rejected frame.  
  vi) A acknowledges the successful reception of the frames after retransmission.  
  vii) B initiates the disconnection, and A acknowledges it.  
3B)               In a digital communication system, a sender uses synchronous transmission while the receiver    (3)  
  uses asynchronous transmission. Describe a scenario where timing errors might occur between the  
  sender and receiver. Illustrate how these timing errors could affect data integrity.  
3C)               We have an available bandwidth of 100 kHz that spans from 200 to 300 kHz. What should be the        (2)  
  carrier frequency and the bit rate if we modulate our data using Quadrature Phase Shift Keying with  
  $$a roll-off factor r=1?$$  
  Page 1 of 2

4A)   Consider a network scenario with four LANs (LAN1, LAN2, LAN3, LAN4) and three transparent                (5)  
  bridges (B1, B2, B3). Stations S1 and S2 are connected to LAN1, S3 and S4 to LAN3, S5 to LAN4,  
  and S6 and S7 to LAN2. The connections are as follows: LAN1 is linked to B1 via port 1 and B2 via  
  port 1; LAN3 is linked to B1 via port 2 and B3 via port 1; LAN4 is linked to B3 via port 2; and LAN2  
  is linked to B2 via port 2. Sequential transmissions occur as follows: S6 to S1, S5 to S4, S3 to S5,  
  S7 to S6, and S6 to S5. Populate the forwarding tables of bridges B1, B2, and B3 with the correct  
  entries after all frames have been transmitted. Give proper justification for each of the given entries.  
4B)   A certain communication system needs to transmit data at a rate of 100 Mbps. Evaluate the signal         (3)  
  rates and minimum bandwidth requirements if digital signal encoding techniques used is  
  Manchester encoding.  
4C)   In what ways does Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing improve spectral efficiency and             (2)  
  reduce inter-symbol interference in communication systems?  
5A)   Consider a communication channel with a bandwidth of 400 kbps, where two systems, one using              (5)  
  Pure ALOHA and the other using Slotted ALOHA, are transmitting 500-bit frames over this shared  
  channel. For the Pure ALOHA system, calculate the throughput when the system generates 1200  
  frames per second, 600 frames per second, and 300 frames per second. Similarly, for the Slotted  
  ALOHA system, calculate the throughput using the same frame generation rates. After performing  
  the calculations, compare the performance of the two protocols under the given conditions. Finally,  
  analyze and explain which system performs better at different traffic levels, discussing why one  
  protocol might be more efficient than the other based on the frame production rates.  
5B)   A system uses the Go-back-N ARQ protocol with a window size of 7. Ignore the overhead due to the (3)  
  header and trailer. (Assume transmission time of frame=1ms). If each frame carries 1000 bits of  
  data, how long does it take to send 1 million bits of data if the distance between the sender and  
  receiver is 5000 Km and the propagation speed is 2 x 108 m? Ignore transmission, waiting, and  
  processing delays. We assume no data or control frame is lost or damaged.  
5C)   Analyze the differences between circuit switching and packet switching with respect to their             (2)  
  communication path and transmission capacity.  
  
  
  -----End-----
